title: Incremental weight onboarder and KV seed coordinator for tenant-priority warmup
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Spike + implementation ticket to build an incremental weight onboarding service and a coordinator that seeds the KV cache in a tenant-prioritized manner. Goal: reduce tenant cold-start P95 latency and stabilize throughput guarantees for Dedicated fleets by introducing a lightweight, admission-friendly onboarding flow that stages weights and proactively inserts hot KV fingerprints. The system must be configurable per-commitment level, respect memory residency budgets, and integrate with the warm-pool controller and autoscaler. This ticket covers design, a first-pass implementation, integration tests, and a canary rollout to a small subset of Dedicated nodes.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarder can stream model weight shards to GPU worker processes in incremental stages without blocking inference for already-resident shards
KV seeder can inject prefix fingerprints for a given tenant so that first inference requests hit the KV cache at >= 65% rate in canary tests
End-to-end cold-start P95 latency for canary tenants reduces by at least 15% vs baseline under representative request traces
Respect per-tenant residency budgets and abort staging when memory pressure is above configured threshold
Telemetry: expose metrics for onboarding progress, staged shard count, KV seed success rate, and eviction incidents
Rollout plan documented and automated with a single PR that wires the feature flag and rollout knobs in the console
design_notes: Adopt an incremental streaming loader: divide weight files into ordered micro-shards and apply them sequentially; workers accept micro-shard patches and update residency metadata

KV seeder will use a tenant fingerprint generator to precompute short prefix keys from recent traffic or synthetic warmup prompts; these fingerprints are pushed to the front of the KV store on targeted workers
Admission controller ties onto the existing warm-pool admission path and will honor a tenant's priority and commitment tier; lower-priority tenants get background-only staging
Graceful fallback: if a worker is under memory pressure or onboarding fails, we surface tenant-level degradation and trigger a fallback to a compatible smaller model variant
Compatibility: must integrate with existing snapshot and delta-snapshot formats (see ENG-30512) and with residency allocator heuristics (see ENG-62041)
Security: KV seeds must not contain PII; seeder will only accept hashed/sanitized fingerprints and will log hashes rather than payloads
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype micro-shard streaming mock in runtime integration harness (owner: Marco) - 3d
Component: onboarder service (stateless coordinator) that orchestrates micro-shard pushes and tracks per-tenant progress
Component: KV seeder module in the runtime agent capable of receiving fingerprint batches and inserting them into local KV caches
API: add admin endpoints for starting/stopping a tenant warmup job and querying progress
Telemetry: add onboarding_progress, kv_seed_insertions_total, kv_seed_success_rate, micro_shard_apply_latency gauges/counters
Tests: unit tests + e2e harness using representative request traces and dedicated canary cluster
PRs: submit separate PRs for runtime change, controller, and console feature flag wiring; coordinate merge order with rollout plan
test_plan: Unit tests for micro-shard assembly and checkpointing semantics
Integration test injecting synthetic fingerprints and asserting KV hits on first real requests
Load test: replay 24h of tenant traffic on a 10-node dedicated canary and compare cold-start P95 to baseline
Chaos test: simulate eviction events and node memory pressure to verify abort/retry logic
Longer soak: run warmup jobs continuously for 72h to validate no memory leakage and stable eviction rate
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime-1.22 feature flag and console toggle
Canary 5% of Dedicated fleets (low-impact tenants) for 1 week, monitor metrics and SLOs
Gradually expand to 25% if no regressions; profile hot paths and optimize micro-shard size
If any of the rollback triggers fire (increased P99 latency, memory-pressure > threshold, unexpected eviction spike), automatically disable warmup and notify oncall
Post-rollout: run a quality evaluation comparing generated outputs for seeded vs unseeded starts to ensure no regression in model outputs
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive KV seeding could evict useful working set -> Mitigation: enforce per-node per-tenant residency caps and admission rate limiting
Risk: onboarding increases GPU memory fragmentation -> Mitigation: stage micro-shards size experiments and monitor fragmentation metrics, fallback to slower rehydration
Risk: seeder introduces noisy telemetry or false positives -> Mitigation: add hashed fingerprint logging and conservative thresholds for success rates
Risk: cross-tenant contamination in shared warm pools -> Mitigation: tenant isolation checks and only allow seeding into nodes with matching tenancy labels
